title: PC Orbit Application Catalogue
description: The applications this product will install, and only these. Every id is a package in Microsoft's winget repository, which hashes what it downloads. The catalogue is the allowlist: an id that is not here never reaches a command (ADR 0006, spec 17.1).

id.description: The winget package identifier, exactly as the repository spells it.

name.description: The product's own name. Never localised: it is what the user looks for on screen and sees again in Add or Remove Programs (spec 21.11).

publisher.description: Who makes it. Shown because 'who am I trusting' is the question before installing anything.

categoryKey.description: i18n key for the group heading.

descriptionKey.description: i18n key for the one line of prose.

installedAs.description: Names this product goes by in Add or Remove Programs, when they differ from `name`. A row counts as installed when one of these equals an installed program's display name or is followed in it by a space - so "Google Chrome" finds "Google Chrome Beta", and "Git" does not find "GitHub Desktop". Omit when `name` is already what Windows shows.

homepage.description: The publisher's own page for the product. Used for two things and nothing else: the Open-site link, and the site's icon, which is the product's real logo when the product is not installed and there is no executable on disk to take it from. HTTPS only.
